phases.message: I'm Marian Oyelaran; I run Larkfield Systems & Services. Start in Noticewick: read the rules, every page of this week's federal solicitations, and open each one for its set-aside, NAICS code and size standard, status and dates. Read only; keep nothing and ask nothing yet.
Bidmoor has Eastmere County's notices. Read the rules and open every notice.
Contractdesk is our own records and policy. Read the policy, every record, and every page of the bid worksheet. Keep nothing yet.
Postwren is our mail. Read every message, the scanned letters too. Don't reply to anyone.
Back in Contractdesk, keep for a bid each solicitation, federal and county, that our policy and the latest amendment let us keep. Keep nothing else.
In Noticewick, send each open question on our worksheet for a federal solicitation we can win, before its questions deadline as the latest amendment states it.

In Bidmoor, send the worksheet's open question for a county notice we can win, if its deadline has not passed. Then tell me, for each solicitation, whether you kept it and sent its question, and why you left the rest alone.

fed_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Noticewick is a stand-in for the federal contract opportunities page. The rules below are FAR Part 19 as the agencies apply it by class deviation (the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul model text), 13 CFR Parts 121 and 125 and SBA's table of size standards effective 17 March 2023, as they stand today. Topics: set-asides, size, subcontracting, questions, amendments.

- Today is Friday 9 October 2026.
- A set-aside is open only to firms of the category the notice names.
- A small business set-aside is for firms small under the size standard of the NAICS code the notice assigns.
- HUBZone, service-disabled veteran-owned (SDVOSB), women-owned (WOSB) and 8(a) set-asides need the firm's SBA certification or designation, shown in SAM;
- a firm's own statement is not enough.
- A notice is Active, Closed (offers were due and are in) or Cancelled (the agency withdrew it).

- Today is Friday 9 October 2026.
- A firm is small if it does not exceed the size standard of the NAICS code the solicitation assigns, the standard in effect when it was issued; the notice states it.
- A receipts standard is measured on average annual receipts: the total over the most recently completed five fiscal years, divided by 5 (13 CFR 121.104).
- An employee standard is measured on the average over the preceding 24 months (121.106).
- One year above the standard does not matter if the average does not exceed it.

- Today is Friday 9 October 2026.
- Under 13 CFR 125.6(a)(1) and clause 52.219-14, a small business awarded a services set-aside (other than construction) agrees that it will not pay more than 50 percent of the amount the government pays it to firms that are not similarly situated.
- For a small business set-aside, a similarly situated firm is a small business; a large business never is.
- A plan that gives a large business more than 50 percent of the price breaks the limit.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Each solicitation's Section L (instructions to offerors) gives its own deadline for questions; the contracting officer answers none received after it. The deadline in the latest amendment governs. Section M states the evaluation factors.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. A solicitation can be amended before offers are due. An amendment can change its set-aside, its dates or its questions deadline. Agencies post amendments here and send them to interested vendors, sometimes by post; the latest one governs, wherever a vendor reads it.

county_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Bidmoor shows Eastmere County's purchasing notices. The county's own purchasing code governs its purchases; federal set-asides and size standards do not apply to them. Topics: vendors, reserved, questions.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. A notice marked Open to all may be bid by any vendor registered with the county. A vendor registers once and renews each year; a registered vendor needs nothing else to propose on an open notice.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. A notice marked Reserved: Local Business Enterprise may be bid only by a vendor registered as an Eastmere County Local Business Enterprise (LBE): a business whose principal office is in Eastmere County. A proposal from any other vendor is returned unread.
Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Each notice gives its own deadline for vendors' questions. The buyer answers none received after it.
